events.label: Birthday tape shows future David in mirror
events.description: At his 17th birthday party, David finds his father's old camcorder, and when he plays the tape of the party there is a impossible glimpse of his future self standing in a mirror behind the room.

events.label: Find DARPA Almanac plans in late father's basement
events.description: Digging in their late father's basement workshop, David and his friends uncover blueprints for a government time machine, complete with all the notes needed to build it.

events.label: Toy-car proof send; neighborhood blackout
events.description: The teens test their homemade device on a toy car, and it vanishes into the past - the power surge blacks out the whole neighbourhood and nearly burns down the basement.

events.label: Quinn past-self feedback nearly erases both
events.description: David hops back a few minutes to stop himself touching the machine, and the two versions of him meeting nearly rip him apart - the same body can't be in two places safely.

events.label: Lottery and wish-fulfillment hops
events.description: Using knowledge of the future, the friends win the lottery and live out wishes they could never afford, jumping back days at a time to cash in.

events.label: Lollapalooza three months back
events.description: The group jumps back three months to attend Lollapalooza, living it up in the past with secret knowledge of everything to come.

events.label: David solo-jumps to fix Jessie confession
events.description: David jumps back alone to undo the moment he confessed to Jessie - and in rewriting that night, breaks her heart all over again from her point of view.

events.label: Plane crash and news disasters escalate
events.description: The kids' meddling starts to show in the news: a plane crashes that never crashed before, and disasters begin mounting wherever their selfish little edits touched.

events.label: Jessie learns truth; friendship fractures
events.description: When Jessie learns David has been secretly rewriting their time together, the trust between the friends shatters and the group starts falling apart.

events.label: Jump to 7th birthday; burn plans and materials
events.description: To undo everything, David jumps back to his 7th birthday and burns his father's plans - stopping the machine ever being built, at the cost of his friendship's history.

events.label: Camera: future David vanishes as timeline rewrites
events.description: On the old camcorder footage, the mysterious future David standing in the mirror fades away - proof that the timeline has finally been rewritten for good.

events.label: Attic: two cameras — party tape + full travel chronicle
events.description: In the attic, David finds two recordings of his birthday: his father's tape, and a full chronicle of the time travels - evidence his older self made it back.

events.label: Future-knowing David reintroduces to Jessie
events.description: The tape ends with a message from the David who survived: the future-knowing boy reintroduces himself to Jessie, hoping to get it right this time.

events.label: Teens find Almanac device
events.description: The teenagers discover the blueprints for the 'Project Almanac' time machine and start building it from spare parts.

events.label: Fix parties / lottery / romance
events.description: With the machine working, the friends use it for small fixes: party do-overs, lottery wins and mended romances.

events.label: Present photographs/reality glitch
events.description: Small edits start to bleed into the present - photographs and memories shift, and reality itself begins to glitch around the travellers.

events.label: Friendship collapse
events.description: The friends turn on each other as the consequences pile up, and their friendship collapses under the weight of everything they've changed.

events.label: Attempt to destroy Almanac
events.description: David makes a final desperate jump to his own seventh birthday to destroy the machine and the plans before any of it can happen.

events.label: Timeline fracture ending
events.description: The story ends with the timeline rewritten: the machine never existed, and only the double camera recording remembers it all.

events.label: Youtube-era butterfly cascade
events.description: Every small change the teens make snowballs - the film plays the 'butterfly effect' out in an age of cameras, phones and online video.

events.label: Jessie romance thread
events.description: Woven through the chaos is David's feelings for Jessie, which his time-hopping keeps accidentally ruining.

ruleEffects.effect: Destroying plans erases machine-using future from birthday tape
Travel chronicle camera remains as residual bootstrap artifact

outcome.summary: Machine unmade; dual-camera coda and knowing flirt imply knowledge or cycle persists.
